music: Instrumental, warm and curious, light piano and pizzicato strings. No vocals. Sits under narration.

scenes.purpose: Make the viewer ask why the page and the shelf disagree
scenes.vo: A shop page says only three left. But the warehouse shelf holds ten. Is the shop wrong?
scenes.title: Only 3 left?

scenes.purpose: Connect to a physical shop: an item in someone's basket is promised
scenes.vo: Think of a real shop. A jacket in another person's basket is still in the shop. But it is not for sale to you. It is promised.
scenes.title: Promised, not free
scenes.sub: In the shop, but not for sale to you.

scenes.purpose: Show the two counts and the subtraction behind the message
scenes.vo: Online, you cannot see the other baskets. So the shop keeps two counts. On hand is what sits on the shelf. Reserved is what is already promised: here, five paid orders not yet shipped, and two shoppers in checkout. Ten minus seven leaves three.
scenes.title: Shelf − promised

scenes.purpose: A checkout hold ends in one of two ways; the count can go up
scenes.vo: Many shops hold an item while you are in checkout. If you pay, it stays reserved until it ships. If you leave, or the time runs out, it goes back, and the count can rise again.
scenes.title: Held, then back
scenes.sub: When a hold starts, and how long it lasts, varies.

scenes.purpose: Two buyers, one item: requests are handled one at a time
scenes.vo: Now two people try to buy the last one at the same moment. A well-built shop takes one request at a time. The first takes the item, and the count drops to zero. The second finds zero, and sees sold out.
scenes.title: One at a time
scenes.sub: First confirmed wins. The second sees sold out.

scenes.purpose: Leave the rule and correct the cart misconception
scenes.vo: So the number you see is the shelf, minus what is promised. In many shops, the cart alone holds nothing. The item is yours when the order is confirmed.
scenes.title: Yours once confirmed
scenes.sub: In many shops, a cart alone holds nothing.
